subject.title: Feature Request: One-click Anthropic authentication (OAuth flow)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic browser OAuth as a first-run onboarding/auth method, and what consent, scope, callback, token-storage, refresh, account-detection, billing, and fallback contract should it use?
rationale: Source inspection shows the helper and provider seams exist, but exposing them as one-click onboarding crosses product UX, provider-policy, and credential-security boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Add Provider-Owned OAuth After Approval
options.body: Expose an additive Anthropic OAuth auth method through the Anthropic plugin after maintainers approve the security, billing, documentation, and fallback contract.

options.title: Keep Explicit Auth Paths
options.body: Keep API-key, setup-token, and Claude CLI as the supported Anthropic setup paths and improve wording or docs instead of adding browser OAuth now.

options.title: Prototype Behind Experimental UX
options.body: Allow a maintainer-owned experimental OAuth path that does not replace current Anthropic setup choices until live provider and security proof are strong.

recommendation.title: Add Provider-Owned OAuth After Approval
recommendation.body: Expose an additive Anthropic OAuth auth method through the Anthropic plugin after maintainers approve the security, billing, documentation, and fallback contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on Anthropic setup-token, Claude CLI, and onboarding-auth metadata decisions.
